findings.detail: The question repeats the problem of M3-S46-T1, which is also in scenario 2. There, values that were correct at different times are misread as contradictions. The correct fix is the same: give each finding the publication or data collection date of its source. The file-timestamp twist does not change the reasoning that leads to A. Two wrong options also repeat. B (keep the figure with the most recent timestamp) matches the earlier 'keep only the official changelog value' option, since both arbitrarily select one value. D (contested section with source attribution) matches the earlier 'list each conflicting value beside its source and flag it as a contradiction' option. The rule allows at most one repeated wrong option.

blind_answer.reason: The dates come from file timestamps, and every file was bulk-copied last month, so all figures look current. Requiring the real publication or data-collection date (5.6-S4) lets the synthesis read figures measured years apart as change over time rather than as conflicting current values. B selects by the same meaningless timestamp. C removes structured metadata. D keeps treating differences that come from timing as genuine conflicts.
